newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to criticize Germany on church issue - W. Post.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to criticize Germany on church issue - W. Post.

text.p: The State Department's annual survey of global human rights conditions will criticise Germany for restrictions on the Church of Scientology and its members, the Washington Post reported on Monday.
The report, to be issued on Wednesday, will chastise Germany for "a campaign of harassment and intimidation" against the church, the newspaper quoted a senior administration official as saying.
The official said the United States had urged Germany through diplomatic channels "not to prosecute people for wrong thinking", but has been rebuffed.
The Church of Scientology filed an application with the European Commission of Human Rights on Friday, accusing the German government of discriminating against its members.

The church says it has documented more than 600 alleged human rights violations by the German government against Scientologists, and the state of Bavaria recently passed a new law banning Scientologists from holding public office.
A German diplomat responded to the State Department report by saying, "We won't change our policy, no matter what you say," the Post said.
"You are a big country. You can afford to have militias and cults. We can't," the diplomat was quoted as saying.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl recently dismissed an open letter from a group of Hollywood stars, including actor Tom Cruise, likening Germany's attitude toward Scientology to the infamous Nuremberg laws against Jews in pre-war Nazi Germany.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the administration felt obliged to support the principle of freedom of worship while remaining critical of statements like the one signed by Hollyhood actors and directors.
"We have criticised the Germans on this, but we aren't going to support the Scientologists' terror tactics against the German government," the Post quoted Burns as saying.
